Laptop and equipment refresh

Company laptops are replaced every 36 months, and a replacement can be requested earlier only when the device is broken or no longer meets the role's needs. Accidental damage is covered once per 12 months; a second incident is charged to the team budget. When someone leaves, all equipment must be returned within 14 days using the prepaid shipping label IT provides.

Employees may keep their old monitor or keyboard at refresh time if IT confirms the item has no company data on it, but laptops and phones must always be returned for secure erasure. Peripherals such a

refresh time if IT confirms the item has no company data on it, but laptops and phones must always be returned for secure erasure. Peripherals such as headsets are reordered through the equipment catalogue up to 150 dollars per year without approval. Equipment bought with a personal card and reimbursed remains company property.

Expense and reimbursement policy

Employees are reimbursed for business expenses that are reasonable and documented. Meals while travelling are capped at 60 dollars per day, and every receipt over 25 dollars must be attached to the expense report. Reports must be submitted within 30 days of the expense or they are not reimbursed. A manager can approve a report up to 500 dollars; anything larger goes to Finance for a second approval. Alcohol, personal entertainment and fines are never reimbursable.

Expenses incurred on a company credit card are reconciled monthly by the cardholder, and unrecon

onal entertainment and fines are never reimbursable.

Expenses incurred on a company credit card are reconciled monthly by the cardholder, and unreconciled transactions older than 60 days are charged back to the employee's department. Client entertainment needs the client's name and the business purpose written on the receipt. For international trips, amounts are converted at the rate on the day of the charge. Questions about a rejected report go to the Finance helpdesk, which answers within two working days.

Onboarding: the first week

A laptop is shipped to new hires five days before the start date, and IT sends login details on day one. Every new hire is assigned an onboarding buddy who is not their manager. Mandatory security training must be completed within 3 days of starting. In the first week the manager shares a 30-60-90 day plan, and the new hire meets each teammate for 20 minutes.

On day one the new hire's accounts for email, chat and the ticketing tool are already created, but access to production systems is granted only after the security training and a signed acceptable use policy. E

ticketing tool are already created, but access to production systems is granted only after the security training and a signed acceptable use policy. Engineers receive repository access on day two after their buddy reviews the setup guide with them. By the end of the first month the new hire presents what they learned to their team in a 15-minute demo.

Performance review cycle

Performance is reviewed twice a year, in June and December. Each review has a self-assessment, manager assessment and feedback from three to five peers chosen with the manager. Ratings use a 1 to 5 scale and are calibrated across teams before they are shared. Promotion decisions are made once a year, in the December cycle, and require at least two consecutive reviews at 4 or above.

A manager who gives a rating of 1 or 2 must write a development plan with specific goals and a follow-up date no later than 90 days later. Employees can see their own feedback but peer com

must write a development plan with specific goals and a follow-up date no later than 90 days later. Employees can see their own feedback but peer comments are shown without names. Compensation changes are decided in a separate meeting after calibration and are announced in January. Anyone who disagrees with a rating can ask for a review by their manager's manager within 10 working days.

Paid time off

Full-time employees receive 25 days of paid time off per year, accrued at 2.08 days per month from the first day of work. Up to 5 unused days carry over into January and anything beyond that expires on 31 January. Time off is requested in Workday; a request longer than 5 consecutive working days needs two weeks of notice. Public holidays are separate and do not use up the allowance.

Sick leave is separate from paid time off: employees have 10 paid sick days per year and need a doctor's note only after 3 consecutive days. Parental leave is 16 weeks at full pay for either parent,

yees have 10 paid sick days per year and need a doctor's note only after 3 consecutive days. Parental leave is 16 weeks at full pay for either parent, and can be taken in blocks within the first year. Unused time off is paid out when employment ends in countries where the law requires it, and otherwise lapses.

Remote work and the home-office stipend

Employees become eligible for fully remote work after 90 days with the company and manager approval. During remote work everyone keeps core hours from 10:00 to 15:00 in their local time zone, when they are expected to be reachable. The company pays a 40 dollar monthly internet stipend and a one-time 300 dollar home-office equipment allowance, claimed through the expense system with the category Remote Setup.

Remote employees must work from the country listed in their contract, because tax and employment rules differ by country; working abroad for more

p.

Remote employees must work from the country listed in their contract, because tax and employment rules differ by country; working abroad for more than 14 days needs written approval from People Operations. Teams meet in person at least once per quarter, and travel for these meetings is budgeted separately. Employees whose home internet is unreliable can ask IT for a mobile hotspot instead of the stipend.

Security awareness rules

Everyone must store passwords in the company password manager and never reuse them. Multi-factor authentication with a hardware security key is required for the admin console and the code repository. Suspected phishing is reported by forwarding the message to the phishing mailbox without clicking anything. A lost or stolen device must be reported to IT Security within 1 hour so it can be wiped remotely.

Customer data may only be stored on company-managed systems; copying it to personal cloud storage or a personal laptop is a policy violation that is reported to the s

y only be stored on company-managed systems; copying it to personal cloud storage or a personal laptop is a policy violation that is reported to the security team. Screens must be locked whenever a device is left alone, and automatic lock is set to 5 minutes. Visitors are signed in at reception and wear a visitor badge, and they are never left alone in the office. Security training is repeated every year.

Booking business travel

Book travel through the company travel portal at least 14 days before departure to get the negotiated fares. Economy class is required for flights under 6 hours; premium economy is allowed above that. Trains are preferred over flying for trips under 4 hours. Hotels are capped at 220 dollars per night in major cities and 150 dollars elsewhere. Changes after booking go through the portal support line, not directly with the airline.

A traveller who must change a trip within 48 hours of departure can phone the travel agency's emergency line, which is open at all hours. Lo

airline.

A traveller who must change a trip within 48 hours of departure can phone the travel agency's emergency line, which is open at all hours. Loyalty points earned on business trips belong to the traveller, but upgrades paid for with points may not be claimed back as expenses. Rental cars are allowed only when public transport is not practical, and the compact class is the default. Per-diem rates for each country are listed in the travel portal.

Writing good alerts

Every alert that pages a human must be actionable, must link to a runbook and must describe a symptom customers feel, not a cause. Alerts that fire without needing action are noisy and are fixed or deleted. The team reviews the ten noisiest alerts every month. A new alert is first sent to a chat channel for two weeks before it is allowed to page anyone.

Dashboards must show the same signals the alerts use, so an engineer paged at night can see what changed. Alert thresholds are set from service-level objectives rather than guesses: a page is raised when the error budget w

ed at night can see what changed. Alert thresholds are set from service-level objectives rather than guesses: a page is raised when the error budget would be exhausted within 6 hours at the current burn rate. Silences for planned maintenance must have an end time and an owner, and silences without an end time are removed automatically after 24 hours.

Backups and restores

Database snapshots are taken every night at 02:00 UTC and kept for 35 days. Point-in-time recovery lets us restore to any second in the last 7 days. A restore is tested every quarter into an isolated environment and the time it takes is recorded; a backup that has never been restored is not considered a backup. Restores of production data require approval from the incident commander.

Backups are encrypted with a key stored in a separate account, and the key access is limited to two named security administrators. Object storage uses versioning with a 90-day retention so a

in a separate account, and the key access is limited to two named security administrators. Object storage uses versioning with a 90-day retention so accidental deletions can be undone. If a restore is needed, the incident commander chooses the recovery point, and the expected restore time for the main database is 90 minutes. Backup job failures raise a ticket automatically.

Capacity planning

Add capacity when average CPU stays above 70 percent for 10 minutes. The platform keeps 30 percent headroom above peak traffic so one availability zone can be lost without an outage. Capacity is reviewed every quarter against the traffic forecast and the cost report. Memory-bound services are scaled on memory, not CPU, and databases are scaled vertically before they are sharded.

Load tests are run before each major launch at 2 times the expected peak, and the results are attached to the launch checklist. Storage is forecast from the last 90 days of growth and extended when

times the expected peak, and the results are attached to the launch checklist. Storage is forecast from the last 90 days of growth and extended when less than 25 percent of free space remains. Cost reviews flag any service whose monthly spend grew more than 20 percent without matching traffic growth, and the owning team explains it in the next review.

Database failover runbook

To fail over the primary database, first confirm the replica's replication lag is under 10 seconds, then promote it with the promote command and wait for it to accept writes. Point the application at the new primary by updating the DNS record, whose TTL is kept at 60 seconds for this reason. The target recovery time is 5 minutes. Afterwards rebuild the old primary as a replica rather than bringing it back as a primary.

Before a planned failover, announce it in the operations channel at least 30 minutes ahead and pause long-running batch jobs, because they would be c

Before a planned failover, announce it in the operations channel at least 30 minutes ahead and pause long-running batch jobs, because they would be cut off when connections move. After the switch, verify that application error rates are normal, that replication to the new replicas has started, and that the connection pool has reconnected. Failover drills are run twice a year in a staging copy of production.

Deploys and rollbacks

Every deploy first goes to a canary receiving 5 percent of traffic for 15 minutes. If the error rate in the canary rises above the baseline the deploy stops automatically. To roll back a bad release run deployctl rollback to the previous version, which takes about 2 minutes. When a service has used 10 percent of its monthly error budget, deploys to it are frozen except for reliability fixes.

Database schema changes must be backwards compatible so a rolled-back release still works with the new schema; destructive changes such as dropping a column are done in a separate r

backwards compatible so a rolled-back release still works with the new schema; destructive changes such as dropping a column are done in a separate release at least one week later. Feature flags are used to switch risky code on gradually, and a flag older than 90 days must be removed. Deploys are not allowed on Fridays after 15:00 unless they fix an active incident.

Incident severity levels

A severity 1 incident is an outage or a problem that stops customers from paying or using the core product. The on-call engineer is paged immediately, an incident commander is named within 10 minutes, and the status page is updated every 30 minutes until resolution. Severity 2 is a major degradation with a workaround, handled during working hours within 4 hours. Severity 3 is a minor defect that goes into the normal backlog.

During a severity 1 incident one person acts as incident commander and does not debug; another engineer is named as communications lead and writ

log.

During a severity 1 incident one person acts as incident commander and does not debug; another engineer is named as communications lead and writes the status updates. Customers affected by a severity 1 incident receive an email within 60 minutes. The incident channel is created from a template, and everything said in it is treated as the record for the later postmortem. An incident is declared resolved only after 30 minutes of stable metrics.

On-call rotation

On-call shifts rotate weekly and hand over every Monday at 10:00 UTC. Each shift has a primary and a secondary engineer; the secondary is paged if the primary does not acknowledge within 5 minutes. The outgoing engineer writes a handoff note listing open incidents, noisy alerts and anything unusual. Swaps are arranged in the paging tool at least 24 hours ahead. Engineers on call receive a day of time off after a week with more than 5 pages.

New engineers shadow the on-call for two weeks before joining the rotation and take their first shift as secondary. If an engineer is un

han 5 pages.

New engineers shadow the on-call for two weeks before joining the rotation and take their first shift as secondary. If an engineer is unreachable during their shift, the manager is paged after 15 minutes and the secondary takes over. Pages outside local working hours are logged so the team can review whether the load is fair. The rotation schedule is published four weeks ahead.

Post-incident reviews

Every severity 1 and severity 2 incident gets a blameless postmortem, written within 5 business days. The document gives a timeline, the impact, the root cause and what went well. A review meeting is held and the action items are entered in the tracker, each with one named owner and a due date. A postmortem is not closed until its action items are done or consciously dropped.

A postmortem lists the contributing factors in plain language and avoids naming individuals, because the aim is to improve the system. Detection time and recovery time are recorded for every incide

plain language and avoids naming individuals, because the aim is to improve the system. Detection time and recovery time are recorded for every incident and reported in a monthly review. Action items that would prevent the same class of incident take priority over feature work, and the engineering director reviews overdue items every two weeks.

Competitive positioning

When a prospect compares us with a competitor, focus on integration depth and total cost, and never disparage the competitor. Our security attestations are SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, and reports are shared under NDA. Common objections and answers are kept in the battlecard for each competitor; reps should update a card when they hear a new objection three times.

Reference customers are matched by industry and size and must give permission before they are shared; the list of approved references is maintained by marketing. Pricing comparisons are never sent in writing

must give permission before they are shared; the list of approved references is maintained by marketing. Pricing comparisons are never sent in writing without approval from product marketing. When a prospect asks about a feature that is on the roadmap, reps may describe the direction but must not promise a date.

Standard contract terms

Contracts are offered for one, two or three years. The standard annual price escalator is 5 percent, and sales may agree to a maximum of 7 percent. Volume pricing steps down at 100 seats and again at 500 seats. Payment terms are net 30 days; net 60 requires finance approval. Auto-renewal is on by default with a 60-day notice window.

Standard terms limit liability to the fees paid in the previous 12 months; any request for a higher cap goes to legal. Customers can add seats at any time at the contracted price, prorated to the end of the term, but reducing seats is only

r a higher cap goes to legal. Customers can add seats at any time at the contracted price, prorated to the end of the term, but reducing seats is only possible at renewal. Data processing terms are included by default for customers in the European Union and signed before the first invoice.

Keeping the CRM accurate

Reps update the opportunity stage within 24 hours of any customer call. Every open opportunity must have a next step with a date. When an opportunity is lost, the loss reason is chosen from the fixed list, not written as free text. Duplicate accounts are merged by sales operations, and reps must not create a new account before searching for an existing one.

The forecast category must match the stage: an opportunity cannot be in commit if no meeting with the economic buyer is recorded. Opportunities with no activity for 30 days are flagged for review and closed as los

ot be in commit if no meeting with the economic buyer is recorded. Opportunities with no activity for 30 days are flagged for review and closed as lost after 60 days unless a next step is logged. Notes from calls are saved in the opportunity, not in personal documents, so a colleague can take over without a handover meeting.

Discount approval

Account executives may offer a discount of up to 10 percent on their own authority. A discount between 10 and 20 percent needs the sales manager's approval, and anything above 20 percent needs the VP of Sales. No discount may take the deal below the 55 percent gross margin floor. Multi-year commitments may earn an additional 3 percent for each extra year, within the same approval limits.

A discount request must include the customer's budget, the competitor being compared, and the planned close date, and approvers answer within one business day. Discounts are never applied t

tomer's budget, the competitor being compared, and the planned close date, and approvers answer within one business day. Discounts are never applied to professional services or training, which are sold at list price. Quarter-end exceptions are not allowed: a deal that needs a discount above the rep's authority after the 25th of the last month needs the VP's approval regardless of size.

Qualifying a lead

Leads are scored against BANT: budget, authority, need and timeline. A score of 70 or more marks a hot lead, which must receive a discovery call within 24 hours. A lead with no budget expected within the next 12 months is disqualified and moved to nurture. The score and the reasons are recorded on the lead so another rep can understand the decision.

Inbound leads from the website are routed round-robin to the sales development team and acknowledged by email within 15 minutes. Leads from existing customers are routed to the account owner instead and are never scored as new b

team and acknowledged by email within 15 minutes. Leads from existing customers are routed to the account owner instead and are never scored as new business. A lead that does not respond after five attempts across two weeks is moved to nurture with a note about the last contact.

Pipeline and forecasting

Opportunities are forecast in three categories: commit, best case and pipeline. The team holds a forecast call every Monday at 09:00, and reps must update their numbers the evening before. Each stage has a default win probability, and managers may adjust it with a written reason. Healthy pipeline coverage is at least three times the quota for the quarter.

Deals with a close date in the current quarter but no activity in the last 14 days are removed from commit. The forecast is submitted by managers by 17:00 on Monday and is compared with the actual closing totals at

the last 14 days are removed from commit. The forecast is submitted by managers by 17:00 on Monday and is compared with the actual closing totals at quarter end to measure accuracy. New logos and expansions are forecast separately because their conversion rates differ. A forecast miss of more than 10 percent is discussed in the next business review.

Quotes

A quote is valid for 30 days from the day it is issued. Quotes use the current price sheet and are created in the CRM, never in a spreadsheet. Any non-standard term, such as custom payment terms or liability caps, needs legal review before the quote is sent. A customer accepts a quote by electronic signature, which creates the order automatically.

A quote shows the term, seat count, unit price, discounts and total in the customer's currency, using the exchange rate set on the first of the month. If the customer requests changes after sending, a new version is created and the old one i

ncy, using the exchange rate set on the first of the month. If the customer requests changes after sending, a new version is created and the old one is marked superseded, so there is only ever one valid quote. Renewal quotes are generated automatically 120 days before the contract end and reviewed by the account owner.

Renewals

Renewal work starts 120 days before the contract ends. The account health score combines product usage, support tickets and executive engagement. At 90 days the rep arranges a meeting with the customer's executive sponsor. Because auto-renewal needs 60 days' notice to cancel, any account still unresolved at 75 days is escalated to the sales manager. Renewals are never discounted without a documented risk.

A renewal quote is sent at 90 days and shows any change in price and in seats. Customers who reduce their seat count are asked for the reason, and the answer is recorded in the CRM

days and shows any change in price and in seats. Customers who reduce their seat count are asked for the reason, and the answer is recorded in the CRM loss reason list. Multi-year renewals are encouraged with a one-time discount of up to 5 percent, and the customer success manager joins the renewal call for accounts above 100,000 dollars a year.

Deleting an account

Only the account owner can delete an account. Deletion starts a 14-day grace period during which the owner can cancel it by signing in. After the grace period the account is closed and the data stays in encrypted backups for 30 more days before it is permanently purged. Once the data is purged it cannot be recovered by anyone, including support.

Deleting an account cancels all active subscriptions and stops future billing, but fees already paid are not refunded unless the refund policy applies. Team members lose access immediately when the deletion starts, and shared proj

ut fees already paid are not refunded unless the refund policy applies. Team members lose access immediately when the deletion starts, and shared projects owned by the account are removed with it. Customers who want to keep their data should request an export before starting the deletion, because exports are unavailable afterwards.

Invoices and billing details

Invoices are generated on the 1st of each month and are available as PDF files under Billing and then Invoices. Only the account owner can change the billing email address. A VAT or tax identification number can be added to the billing profile, and it appears on invoices issued after the change but is not applied retroactively. Failed payments are retried three times over seven days before the account is suspended.

Customers who need an invoice reissued in a different company name can ask for a corrected copy within 30 days of the original date; after that, accou

Customers who need an invoice reissued in a different company name can ask for a corrected copy within 30 days of the original date; after that, accounting rules do not allow changes. Credit notes are issued for refunds and appear in the same list as invoices. Enterprise customers can pay by bank transfer with a purchase order number printed on every invoice.

Data export requests

An account owner can request a full export of the account's data. Exports are produced as CSV or JSON files and delivered within 72 hours through a secure download link that stays valid for 7 days. The request must come from the verified account owner; an agent cannot approve an export on behalf of a regular user. Large exports above 50 GB are split into several files.

Exports include users, projects, files and activity logs, but not billing card details, which are never stored by the company. Customers on the Pro plan and above can schedule a recurring export every week

s, but not billing card details, which are never stored by the company. Customers on the Pro plan and above can schedule a recurring export every week to their own storage bucket. If an export fails, the customer receives an email with a reference number and the team retries it automatically twice before contacting them.

Escalating a ticket

A Tier-1 agent escalates to Tier-2 when a ticket has not been resolved after 2 hours of work or needs an account-level change. A severity 1 problem skips Tier-2 and pages the on-call engineer directly. Every escalation must include the account name, the steps already tried, the customer's exact error text and the time the customer first reported it. The customer is told who now owns the ticket.

A Tier-2 agent who cannot resolve a ticket within one working day opens an engineering ticket and links it to the customer ticket so progress can be tracked from either side. Engin

lve a ticket within one working day opens an engineering ticket and links it to the customer ticket so progress can be tracked from either side. Engineering fixes are communicated back through the support agent, never directly to the customer. If a customer asks to speak to a manager, the agent offers a call within one business day and records the request in the ticket.

Webhook delivery and retries

Webhooks are sent as signed HTTP POST requests. A delivery that does not receive a 2xx response is retried 5 times with exponential backoff, for up to 1 hour in total, and then marked failed. Each request carries an HMAC-SHA256 signature computed with the endpoint's signing secret, which customers should verify. Customers who restrict inbound traffic can allow the published webhook IP ranges.

Webhook endpoints must respond within 10 seconds, or the delivery counts as failed and is retried. Events are delivered at least once, so receivers must tolerate duplicates

respond within 10 seconds, or the delivery counts as failed and is retried. Events are delivered at least once, so receivers must tolerate duplicates by checking the event identifier in the payload. After 20 consecutive failures an endpoint is disabled automatically and the account owner is emailed; re-enabling it is done from the integrations page.

Resetting a password

Customers reset their own password with the Forgot password link on the sign-in page. The reset link is valid for 30 minutes and works once. After 5 failed sign-in attempts the account is locked for 15 minutes. Customers who sign in through single sign-on cannot reset a password here; they must contact their company's identity administrator. Agents must never ask a customer to tell them their password.

If a customer never receives the reset email, the agent first checks the spam folder advice, then confirms the address on the account, and finally asks the customer to wai

eceives the reset email, the agent first checks the spam folder advice, then confirms the address on the account, and finally asks the customer to wait 10 minutes before requesting another link, because several requests invalidate the older ones. Customers who have lost access to their email address must verify their identity with the account owner or a government identity document before the address can be changed.

Refund policy

Customers can request a full refund within 30 days of the first purchase. After 30 days, annual plans are refunded pro rata for the unused full months, and monthly plans are not refunded. Approved refunds are returned to the original payment method within 5 to 7 business days. Refunds above 1,000 dollars, and any exception to these rules, must be approved by a Tier-2 agent before the customer is told the outcome.

Refunds for add-on services, such as extra storage or premium support, follow the same 30-day window but are calculated from the date the add-on was activated, not fro

n services, such as extra storage or premium support, follow the same 30-day window but are calculated from the date the add-on was activated, not from the first purchase. Chargebacks opened with a bank before a refund request are handled by the billing team, not by support agents. When a refund is granted the agent adds the reason code to the ticket so finance can report on it, and sends the customer a confirmation email with the amount.

Support plans and response times

Basic plans receive a first response within 24 business hours. Pro plans receive a first response within 8 business hours. Enterprise plans receive a first response within 1 hour at any time, every day of the year. A severity 1 problem means the product is unusable for the whole account and is treated as Enterprise priority on every plan. Response time is measured to the first human reply, not to the automatic acknowledgement.

Business hours for first-response targets are 08:00 to 18:00 on weekdays in the customer's region, excluding public holidays. A ticket

knowledgement.

Business hours for first-response targets are 08:00 to 18:00 on weekdays in the customer's region, excluding public holidays. A ticket that breaches its target is flagged to the team lead and must be answered within 30 minutes. Customers upgrading mid-month are moved to the new tier immediately, and the response targets apply from the moment the upgrade is confirmed in billing.

LangGraph: Graph Model

LangGraph models an app as a stateful graph of nodes and edges. Conditional edges let the agent loop between an LLM node and a tool node.

LangGraph: Checkpointers

A LangGraph checkpointer (like MemorySaver) persists state per thread_id, giving the agent conversation memory across turns.

Qdrant: Payloads and Filtering

Qdrant stores vectors with JSON payloads. You can filter searches by payload fields, for example restricting results to a single topic.

Qdrant: Similarity Metrics

Cosine distance is a common similarity metric for text embeddings in Qdrant.

Ecorp: About

Ecorp was founded in 2021 and builds offline developer tools. Its flagship product is a local AI stack starter kit.

Ecorp: Support Hours

Ecorp's support hours are 9am to 5pm on weekdays, and support is free for all open-source users.

deal-economics

deal-economics: Compute real multi-year deal math a plain calculator can't do — escalating annual pricing, volume-discount tiers, total contract value. Use when a lead is negotiating anything beyond a flat single-year price.

expense-summary

expense-summary: Summarize and total a list of expense line items into a reimbursement-ready report. Use when the user pastes expense line items, receipts, or costs and wants them summed, categorized, or formatted as an expense report.

onboarding-brief

onboarding-brief: Compose a new-hire onboarding brief for an Ecorp employee. Use when the user asks for an onboarding brief, a welcome packet, a new-hire summary, or wants to prep for someone's first day.

ops-incident-response

ops-incident-response: Run a full ops investigation end to end — pull current metrics, check whether it's happened before, log a real anomaly as an incident, and resolve it once it's fixed. Use for "why is X happening", "did anything break", or any request to investigate this app's own operational health.

sales-lead-qualification

sales-lead-qualification: Work an inbound lead from first contact through qualification to a clean outcome — scheduled follow-up, handoff to a human rep, or marked lost. Use for any inbound sales/CRM message, not just ones that already show obvious buying intent.

support-log-triage

support-log-triage: Parse a customer-pasted error log, stack trace, or webhook/JSON payload for real facts — occurrence counts, exception types, whether JSON is even well-formed — instead of eyeballing raw pasted text. Use whenever a customer pastes a log dump, error message, or payload and asks what it means or how often something happened.

support-tier1-triage

support-tier1-triage: Triage an inbound customer support request end to end — check the knowledge base first, open a ticket if unresolved, escalate to a human when it's outside Tier-1 scope. Use for any customer issue, complaint, or question arriving through the support copilot.

vendor-incident-postmortem

vendor-incident-postmortem: Investigate whether an anomaly is caused by an external vendor/dependency, with real evidence — not a guess. Use when fetch_metrics_summary flags something and a vendor is a plausible cause, or when someone directly asks "is this our fault or theirs."
